alternatives.concept: Social, developmental, clinical and cognitive psychology are studied through empirical research and evidence synthesis. Organisational psychology, biological foundations, behavioural economics and social theory add distinct perspectives on people, mental processes and social settings.

alternatives.label: Brain, cognition & mind
alternatives.concept: Brain and behaviour, perception, memory and language form the centre of this programme. Neuroscience and psychology connect with data analysis and computational models of vision, while philosophy examines consciousness, emotion and the self.
alternatives.distinctness: The organising inquiry is cognition and mind. Specific computational/data and philosophy-of-mind courses replace organisational and sociological study; normal physiology supports the biological strand. General molecular pathology, broad anatomy and biochemical laboratory courses have been removed because they did not implement this concept closely enough. Pairwise numerical differences are verified separately.

alternatives.labelReason: The label reflects substantial cognitive neuroscience and psychology together with explicit philosophy-of-mind and computational perspectives; it does not claim that all courses teach neuroscience.

alternatives.label: Psychology, leadership & organisations
alternatives.concept: Psychology of work and organisations connects with leadership, diversity, negotiation, behavioural decision-making and empirical research. Sociology and business courses examine the institutional settings in which people work.
alternatives.labelReason: The broader label reflects the completed mix of psychology, leadership, organisations, sociology, communication, business and behavioural economics.
alternatives.distinctness: Organisational psychology and leadership replace the biological and cognitive emphasis.

candidates.label: A Brain and Cognition route centred on cognitive neuroscience, perception, higher-order functions, language, biological foundations and quantitative/data-oriented research.

A Work and Organisational Psychology route centred on organisational behaviour, leadership, diversity, negotiation, workplace wellbeing, behavioural decision-making and applied organisational research.
A clinical-psychology and mental-health direction centred on psychological disorders, diagnosis, assessment and clinically relevant behaviour.
An educational-psychology and learning direction centred on learning, motivation, cognition and educational application.

routeSelection.basis: The official programme distinguishes fundamental Brain & Cognition from three applied directions. Retain the fundamental continuation of the common biological/cognitive core for this generic target; it is also first-listed in the adopted EER. Selection is independent of UCR availability.

selection.assessment: Threeconcepts pass sequentially fromsubstantialpsychological theory, empiricalmethods andspecificapplications. Broadpsychology retains developmental,clinical,social,cognitive andorganisationalstudy. Cognition/mindadds genuine neural,computational andphilosophicaltools; work/organisationsadds directleadership/emotion-regulation/negotiation andspecificinstitutional contexts. Both are qualitativelydistinct andexceed30ECfloor. Clinical andeducationcandidates remain recordedmaximum-reached onlyafter threevalidprogrammes.

notes.text: The Erasmus curriculum includes specialist psychological assessment, psychometrics, professional skills and a required 14-EC thesis. These UCR programmes offer related academic study and do not establish the same specialist preparation or automatic access to a particular master’s programme.

audience.programmeDescription: Psychology at Erasmus University Rotterdam studies behaviour, emotion, development and cognition through psychological theory, research methods and practical training. The pathway shown continues through Brain & Cognition after the shared core.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers a broad psychology programme and two related options focusing on cognition and mind, or psychology and organisations. They share substantial psychological inquiry with Erasmus, while adding other disciplines. Dedicated psychometrics, specialist professional training and the compulsory 14-EC thesis are not reproduced.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC include a 15-EC approved minor and two programme-offered psychology electives of 5 EC each. Erasmus also requires test-subject hours without EC. Lectures are in English; the Dutch track uses Dutch tutorials and examinations.

componentNotes.psy-elective: 10 EC of psychology profiling: two programme-offered 5-EC electives, one five-week and one nine-week course; places may be limited.
componentNotes.psy-minor: 15 EC of approved minor or exchange space.
componentNotes.psy-thesis: Required 14-EC thesis. Optional UCR independent research is additional and unscheduled.
